questions.question: What does the Society of Minds protocol have N model instances do?
options: Each independently runs a different benchmark suite and reports separate scores without cross-reading
Independently propose answers, then over R rounds read and critique each other's proposals until they converge
Each trains on a shared dataset assembled from the other instances' prior transcripts and logs
Each negotiates a shared compute budget before any proposals are generated or read at all
questions.explanation: N proposers, R rounds, cross-critique, convergence is the canonical Du et al. debate.

questions.question: Why does cross-model debate (e.g. ChatGPT + Bard) outperform single-model debate?
options: Different vendors negotiate lower API prices when their models are combined in one pipeline
It is cheaper because mixed-vendor requests are billed at a discounted combined rate
Heterogeneity reduces shared blind spots so cross-critique catches more errors
The vendors share model weights internally once a debate session begins
questions.explanation: Mixing models brings independent error distributions, which raises the ceiling of debate.

questions.question: What is the main token-cost win of a sparse topology over full mesh?
options: Sparse topology requires no models at all, replacing debate entirely with a single deterministic rule
Sparse topology doubles the number of rounds so every debater eventually sees every peer
It removes the LLM entirely and routes proposals through a fixed lookup table instead
Each debater reads only a subset of peers, so critique-op count drops while accuracy often matches
questions.explanation: Sparse (star, ring, hub-and-spoke) reduces critique ops without losing accuracy on many tasks.

questions.question: Which case does the lesson list as where debate hurts?
options: A simple factual lookup, because one lookup is cheaper than five debates
Open-ended reasoning tasks where multiple framings help narrow in on the right answer
Chess move validity checks where one model catching a missed rule matters most
Biography generation tasks that benefit from independent cross-checked proposals
questions.explanation: Latency- and cost-sensitive trivial lookups do not benefit from N x R debate.

questions.question: What is convergence collapse?
options: A network outage that drops the connection between debating agents mid-round
All agents converge on the first wrong answer; mitigate with required disagreement rounds
A process crash in the orchestrator that halts the debate before convergence
A TLS handshake failure between the agent and its model provider's API endpoint
questions.explanation: Early agreement on a wrong answer is mitigated by forcing distinct round-1 proposals.

questions.question: Why does prompt homogenization undermine debate?
options: It violates the Apache 2.0 license terms that most debate frameworks ship under
It uses too many tokens because identical prompts are never cached by the provider
Identical prompts produce nearly identical answers, removing the cross-critique signal
It bypasses the supervisor's routing logic, sending proposals directly between all peer agents
questions.explanation: Diverse prompts (and ideally diverse models) keep the proposal distribution wide.
